title: Kortyx Cookies and Similar Storage Notice

sections.title: 1. Scope
sections.text:
Kortyx uses browser storage for requested website features, sign-in and Cloud operation. This notice explains the mechanisms and their purposes. Broader data uses, recipients and request rights are in the [Website Privacy and Software Telemetry Notice](https://kortyx.io/privacy/v1.1) and [Cloud Privacy Notice](https://kortyx.io/cloud/privacy/v1). Contact legal@kortyx.io about storage or privacy choices.

A cookie can be sent automatically with relevant browser requests. Local storage remains in the browser until cleared; session storage normally ends with the relevant tab/session. A random identifier can still relate to identifiable activity. Browser expiry is distinct from retention of server records or information already received by a provider.

sections.title: 2. Website storage
sections.text:
The website stores necessary privacy choices and requested display/navigation settings. Optional PostHog, Google Analytics 4 and Cloudflare Web Analytics load only after you accept “Website analytics.” Accept and reject are available in the banner; the footer's “Privacy settings” lets you change the choice. Ordinary public content works after rejection. An earlier necessary-only acknowledgment does not authorize the optional category.

| Name or mechanism | Purpose and provider | Persistence and scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kortyx_privacy_v2` cookie and related local storage | c15t remembers this browser's accept/reject choice, identifier and timestamp; no Cloud Terms acceptance | Preference validity/cookie duration 180 days; related local storage remains until cleared. Host-specific, without cross-subdomain sharing |
| Legacy `kortyx_privacy` preference storage | Earlier necessary-only notice acknowledgment; never imported as analytics consent | May remain from an earlier release; former cookie duration 180 days, local storage until cleared |
| `theme` local storage | Requested light/dark appearance | Until changed or cleared |
| Documentation navigation session storage | Sidebar position and expanded/collapsed sections | Browser session/tab; not a marketing identifier |
| `_ga`, `_ga_3BQH1L8V4K` cookies | Optional Google Analytics browser/session measurement | Configured expiry 180 days, not renewed on activity; scoped to kortyx.io. Actual lifetime can be shortened by browser rules or withdrawal |
| PostHog in-memory identifiers | Optional page-view measurement and navigation within the current document | Document-memory lifetime only; no PostHog analytics cookie or persistent local-storage identity |
| Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon | Optional public-page performance and view measurement | No analytics cookie or persistent visitor identifier |

The same optional category controls these three website measurement services. No session replay, advertising pixel, Google Tag Manager container or LinkedIn tag is installed. First-party naming does not make analytics necessary. Cloudflare automatic injection is disabled; the site controls loading through the preference.

sections.title: 3. Cloud and authentication storage
sections.text:
| Mechanism | Purpose | Duration or governing session |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `__Host-kortyx_session` | Opaque reference to the requested authenticated Cloud session | Browser-session cookie; the server can expire or revoke the session independently |
| `__Host-kortyx_login` | Binds a sign-in transaction and protects its return flow | Short-lived transaction, normally five minutes; cleared when completed or restarted |
| `__Host-kortyx_logout` | Binds the sign-out return flow | Up to five minutes, then cleared or expired |
| `__Host-kortyx_workspace`, `__Host-kortyx_project` | Remembers the user’s selected workspace/project context | Up to 30 days; access is still checked server-side |
| `kortyx.cloud.analytics.v1` local storage | Stores this browser’s separate allow/reject choice for optional Cloud product analytics; no account or Terms acceptance identity | Valid for 180 days; missing/invalid/expired choices default to off and are requested again |
| Keycloak authentication cookies | Maintain the identity-provider authentication transaction, authenticated SSO session and requested “Remember me” behavior | Transaction/session dependent. Current realm session policy has 30-minute idle and ten-hour maximum standard sessions; “Remember me” uses seven-day idle and 30-day maximum sessions. Cookie expiry and a server session’s validity are separate |

Cloud application cookies are scoped to the application host; identity-provider cookies are scoped to its authentication host. Production and staging use different hosts and stores. Authentication cookies use the protections appropriate to their purpose; the `__Host-` cookies are host-bound, secure and HTTP-only. Internal Admin has its own authenticated session and staff authorization and is not granted by customer cookies.

The identity-provider cookie names and compatibility variants can depend on the active sign-in flow and browser. They include authentication-session, restart and SSO/remember-me mechanisms. They do not grant permission to use customer content for analytics. A successful identity-provider session does not replace required application authorization or the current contractual acceptance check.

sections.title: 4. Product analytics and distributed software
sections.text:
After the separate browser choice allows it, Cloud usage instrumentation can use `kortyx.usage.id` in local storage to hold a random pseudonymous browser identifier; it persists until cleared, with an in-memory fallback where storage is unavailable. Rejecting or withdrawing disables browser capture, discards queued unsent aggregates and removes the stored Cloud usage identifier. The choice is available in Account settings. Self-hosted Studio has its own operator controls and is not silently changed by a Cloud preference. The provider destination is PostHog Cloud EU. Measurements use fixed operation/feature categories and bounded aggregates rather than customer prompts, outputs or trace bodies. Session replay and automatic page-content capture are outside this release.

This is product analytics, separate from storage necessary for sign-in. Where consent is required, optional browser collection must remain off until the relevant choice and stop after withdrawal. An operator-wide environment opt-out is not a substitute for a browser user’s required choice. Before enabling optional browser collection that requires consent, Kortyx will provide an effective Cloud-specific choice and withdrawal control. The website privacy dialog controls only website analytics, and does not control Cloud analytics.

SDK/CLI telemetry does not necessarily use a browser. Its installation identifier and `KORTYX_USAGE_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` control are described in Website Privacy section 5. Changing a website cookie preference does not change software running on an independent computer or server.

sections.title: 5. Optional choices and browser controls
sections.text:
Rejecting website analytics keeps vendor scripts off. Withdrawing through the footer's “Privacy settings” stops future website capture, clears Google Analytics cookies and reloads to remove active vendor code. The saved rejection persists across the reload. This does not erase records already received by a provider; use legal@kortyx.io for applicable requests. No cross-device synchronization is promised. Clearing browser storage, using another device or starting a private session may require a new choice.

Browser settings can inspect, delete or restrict cookies and local storage. Blocking a necessary authentication mechanism may prevent sign-in. Deleting a cookie alone does not close an account, revoke every device session or erase server-side contractual evidence. Use the relevant account/session controls or the private request channel for those actions.

If a browser or applicable law provides an additional privacy signal or opt-out right, we will assess and honor the obligation applicable to that processing. We do not represent a technical integration for an unimplemented browser signal merely by stating that rights are preserved.

sections.title: 6. Separate records and purposes
sections.text:
Cloud Terms acceptance records the affirmative agreement to a specific document version and hash on the server. Website privacy preferences concern browser mechanisms. Optional onboarding answers concern understanding customer needs. Promotional subscriptions have separate permission and withdrawal. None of these can silently substitute for another.

The expiry of a preference or session cookie does not establish physical deletion of all associated information. The privacy notices describe analytics, security, correspondence, acceptance and backup retention and the applicable request rights. A provider may receive network metadata during a request even where the request contains no browser cookies.

sections.title: 7. Changes and contact
sections.text:
Before enabling a new optional service, replay feature, tracking pixel or materially different purpose, Kortyx will update the relevant disclosure and obtain any required choice. The optional services and controls in this version describe the website analytics rollout; search-management tools do not automatically install a visitor beacon. A revised notice alone is not renewed consent.

Published versions remain identifiable through permanent links. For questions or a request, email legal@kortyx.io without including passwords, session-cookie values, authentication codes or unnecessary identity documents.
